links.outcome: Recognition of red-flag conditions (multiple myeloma, metastatic spinal tumor) and residual safety-risk errors
links.effect: MM recognition improved only from 45% to 55% (DeepSeek V3.2) and 55% to 60% (ChatGPT 5.1); structured input reduced safety-risk errors but residual errors remained, especially MM and metastatic spinal tumor.
links.quote: Structured input reduced safety-risk errors in both models, but residual errors remained, especially for MM and metastatic spinal tumor.

links.outcome: Triage and preliminary diagnosis accuracy of LLMs as potential stand-alone tools
links.effect: Suboptimal red-flag sensitivity; preliminary diagnosis accuracy 76.7% (DeepSeek) and 87.5% (ChatGPT) with structured input; authors state models should not be used stand-alone without clinician oversight.
links.quote: However, their suboptimal sensitivity for red-flag conditions such as MM highlights significant safety concerns, indicating that they should not be used as stand-alone triage tools without clinician oversight.

unlisted_practices: Providing structured clinical questionnaire input versus chief-complaint-only input to improve LLM triage and diagnostic accuracy

screen.reason: The study empirically tests the diagnostic and triage performance of LLMs using real outpatient records across two information conditions (structured clinical questionnaire input vs. chief complaint alone), evaluating how input structuring impacts accuracy and safety-risk errors.

primary.practice: structured clinical questionnaire input vs unstructured chief complaint
